# i18n and user-facing text

Full rules: [packages/i18n/README.md](../../packages/i18n/README.md), terminology and tone: [GLOSSARY.md](../../packages/i18n/GLOSSARY.md), ADR-008.

- Every user-facing string comes from `packages/i18n/{nl-NL,en}.json`. No literals in JSX, `alt`/`title`/`placeholder`/`aria-*`, `metadata`, email templates, Swift or Kotlin. The Biome plugin misses strings outside JSX, so check those yourself.
- Add each key to **both** catalogs in the same change. Dutch is the source language; use the glossary's NL and EN terms.
- Keys: dot paths grouped by screen or feature, lowerCamelCase segments, at least two segments, named after the English glossary term (`booking.spotsAvailable`). Email copy goes under `email.*`.
- Supported ICU only: `{name}` placeholders and at most one cardinal `plural` with exactly `one` and `other`. No `=0`/`=1`, `select`, `selectordinal`, `{n, number}`, `{d, date}` or rich-text tags; use a separate key instead.
- Format dates, times and numbers in code (`dateTimeFormats`, workspace time zone, default Europe/Amsterdam) and pass the result as a plain placeholder. `en` formats as `en-GB`.
- After editing a catalog: `pnpm --filter @fivvi/i18n generate`, commit `generated/`, then `pnpm check`. Never edit `generated/` by hand.
- Before pushing, run the local copy review (`GLOSSARY.md`) on every new or changed string.
